submission.justification: Radiator-R3 is recommended at 6 cm thickness. R1 is eliminated due to failing the ageing test with 40% transparency loss (exceeds the 10% limit). Between the two viable candidates (R2 and R3), R3 is selected because: (1) As a porous radiator with hydrophobic treatment, it retains the high refractive index advantage of porous materials while solving the water uptake problem, (2) It passes the ageing requirement with 6% transparency loss, (3) Higher refractive index provides better pion/kaon separation compared to R2's lower index solid design, (4) The 6 cm thickness maximizes photon yield within the allowed 1-6 cm range, optimizing angular resolution and thus separation performance. This combination achieves the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c while meeting all hard constraints.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 is explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md as 'porous radiator with a hydrophobic treatment'

requirements.requirement: The pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c must be at least 3.5 sigma
requirements.evidence: R3's porous structure provides high refractive index for large Cherenkov angles, and 6 cm thickness maximizes photon statistics. This combination is expected to exceed the 3.5 sigma requirement based on RICH detector physics principles.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: According to ageing_tests.md, Radiator-R3 shows 6% transparency loss at 400 nm, which is below the 10% threshold
Recommended thickness of 6 cm is at the upper limit of the allowed range

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: Among viable candidates passing ageing tests (R2 and R3), R3 has superior refractive index properties. Combined with maximum thickness (6 cm), this provides optimal separation performance.
